source.title: Iterative Normalization: Beyond Standardization Towards Efficient Whitening
source.authors: Lei Huang; Yi Zhou; Fan Zhu; Li Liu; Ling Shao

record.file_problem: Full paper text provided; no apparent cutoff or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares normalization methods on training performance, including BN against a network without normalization, using MNIST rather than the benchmarks and architectures in V6.
record.gate_note: Only the MNIST MLP comparison of BN with a plain network directly bears on V6. The CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments compare IterNorm with BN and DBN, not BN with an otherwise identical network without normalization. Mentioned results from cited studies are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares BN with an unnormalized MNIST MLP and reports a batch-size-dependent reversal of BN's training benefit, bearing on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the micro-batch conclusion but omits the paper's main conclusion: IterNorm improves optimization and generalization over BN and computational efficiency over DBN. The authors use normalization disturbance and conditioning to explain batch-size and dimension effects, including BN's optimization difficulty with undersized batches.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies IterNorm, an iterative whitening method, and compares it with BN, DBN and a plain network in selected experiments; it does not reproduce the source studies' BN experiments as specified in V6.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size: in the MNIST MLP experiments, BN improves performance with full-batch gradient but has difficulty learning with batch size 2.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic-data experiments measure normalization disturbance and covariance conditioning as batch size and feature dimension vary.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN's stochastic normalization disturbance increases with smaller batches and higher feature dimensions; these measurements alone do not establish training speed.

record.problems: The MNIST MLP training comparisons are presented in figures without reported numeric values or uncertainty. The paper says results are averaged over 3 runs for its CIFAR-10 setup, but does not state that this applies to the MNIST comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No other results directly compare BN with an otherwise identical network without BN. CIFAR-10 and ImageNet results compare IterNorm with BN and DBN, and are not rows for V6's BN-versus-no-normalization claim.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error across model sizes, corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, early stopping and regularization recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima and additional student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization-dependent training speed, gradient propagation and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature changes, loss recovery and divergence.
Higher learning-rate tolerance relative to an unnormalized counterpart; Fixup; the original sigmoid, VGG and Inception comparisons. The MNIST MLP's activation is not specified in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V6. Comparisons of IterNorm with BN or DBN do not establish BN's benefit over no normalization. Figure-only numeric values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Training error under random labels, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 overfitting, model size, early stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima and student width.
Depth effects with and without residual shortcuts; special initializations and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training above stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness and divergence.

The experiments test an MLP on MNIST, not the listed sigmoid networks, VGG on CIFAR-10 or Inception on ImageNet. They do not test BN's tolerance of higher learning rates against a no-BN counterpart, nor Fixup.

rows.note: The text says all normalization methods significantly improve performance; the plotted training errors compare the methods with the plain network.
rows.check: Figure 3(a) reports training classification error, with test error shown separately. Curves use each method's best training-loss result among the listed learning rates; this supports faster progress under tuned rates, not a matched-learning-rate comparison. Exact values are unavailable in the supplied text.

statements.correction: Figure 3(b), Section 4.3: four-layer MNIST MLP; 100 neurons per hidden layer; batch size 2; separately selected learning rates; training loss only; BN barely learns while the plain network learns well. CIFAR-10 experiments use VGG with 16 convolutional layers and one fully connected layer, comparing BN, DBN and IterNorm.
statements.problem: The MNIST comparison is accurate. This study does not report a five-layer CIFAR-10 CNN versus vanilla control at batch size 2 or CIFAR-10 failures at batch size 1.

statements.correction: Figure 3: BN improves full-batch MNIST training but barely learns at batch size 2. Section 5.1 and Figure 6: CIFAR-10 VGG comparisons include batch size 16; IterNorm converges faster than BN and DBN; no plain-network control or BN training failure is reported there.
statements.problem: The MNIST findings are accurate. CIFAR-10 failure relative to an unnormalized control is not established here; its small-batch CIFAR-10 experiment compares normalization methods. UNet and single-example fitting claims concern other studies.
